title: Zutty Singleton and Baby Lovett
summary: Jones says he missed Zutty on the circuit and calls Baby Lovett the best-looking drummer behind a set.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Hey, what about Zutty? Now that's an old man; that's about when I came in, Zutty.

...I knew of Zutty and I was told about Zutty. I missed Zutty because Zutty had left by the time I was traveling around on circuses and carnivals, through Shreveport and playing the Star Theatre and what have you.
He's perhaps the senior senator of drums.

He's a Senior Citizen but you must remember, I call him Mr. Kansas City. He's a fellow by the name of Baby Lovett. There is not one man that I know of that looks better behind a set of drums than Baby Lovett, unless

it's Sonny Greer. But nobody looks behind a set of drums - he can just sit behind a set of drums and he will remind you of Jimmy Fox, Jimmy Fox the baseball player, that looked like a baseball. Well, Mr. Lovett looks like drums, you see, and I'm speaking in the jazz idiom.
